newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Lower offers into Saudi tender.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Lower offers into Saudi tender.

text.p: Gasoline prices were unchanged despite weaker crude as sentiment was supported by talk of Saudi Aramco buying the full volume of 1.5 million barrels it tendered for in April, traders said on Tuesday.
Traders said sellers into Aramco's tender for 95-octane leaded gasoline have lowered their offers to $3-$5 per barrel over Singapore naphtha fob quotes.
On Monday, they said the national oil company was shocked at the high cost-and-freight Ras Tanura offers at a $6-$8 premium and were considering to buy less than a million barrels.
In the Singapore fob market, a European major sold 50,000 barrels of 92-octane unleaded mogas to a Dutch trader at $28.55 per barrel for March 28-April 1 lifting.
The buyer then re-emerged with a higher bid of $28.70 for the same timing. On Monday, the grade was offered at $28.80.
Unleaded 97-octane was offered at $29.70 for March 29-April 10 lifting, traders said.
On the outlook, they said the prompt tightness was easing, and prices were set to ease.
"They are among the highest compared to the rest of the world, and if barrels come here, there is no outlet," said an anxious trader.
Naphtha edged down slightly, largely discounting crude's fall. April swaps were quoted at $23.00/$23.05 per barrel, compared to $23.00/$23.20 on Monday.
But the backwardation on April/May paper widened slightly to just below 65 cents per barrel with May talked at $22.35/$22.45, down from Monday's $22.40/$22.60.
